findings.text: In its first paragraph the page says what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. A newcomer can say what it is and why it matters without reading further.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The next step is linked from the top of the page. The Next steps section gives prerequisites, a clone command, `./setup.sh` and a first `athena ask "add a changelog"` command. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: The page describes two things Athena does: it turns requests into commits, and it writes studies like this one. It never says how the two fit together. Next steps only shows `athena ask`, so a newcomer who liked this study does not learn how to make one.
findings.source: header lede: "turns a short request into a change to a code repository" vs. "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project"

findings.text: This is Athena's home page, but almost all of it is a detailed study of another project, firstmate. "Start here" explains firstmate, not how to start with Athena, so a newcomer who came for Athena may think they are on the wrong page.
findings.source: title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the "Start here" heading

findings.text: A newcomer is not an owner and is not told whose proposals these are. This link at the top is unexplained and may confuse them.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: "Verdict" is never defined. A newcomer can guess that it is the checking model's judgment, but the page does not say so.
findings.source: header lede: "a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict"

findings.text: The firstmate material is careful and every statement is traced to a claim. It is far deeper than a newcomer needs, but it does show what Athena can do, which the lede says is its purpose.
findings.source: Transitions section, cards t1–t12, and Claims and sources (45 claims)

findings.text: This section points to an internal repository folder without saying which repository it means. It tells a newcomer nothing they can use.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
